paragraphs: In Torfaen the council's fostering service is Foster Wales Torfaen, based at the Civic Centre in Pontypool and part of the national network of 22 not-for-profit council fostering services in Wales. Children from Pontypool, Cwmbran and the surrounding communities are looked after by its carers and by the services shown above.

Foster Wales Torfaen looks for carers for babies, toddlers, teenagers, brothers and sisters, and young parents, with care that can be as short as one night or as long as a permanent home. Teenagers are a particular focus: in January 2026 the council ran a campaign for carers who can give older children a stable home close to their family, school and friends. The council also supports kinship carers, parent and child placements, supported lodgings for young people, and a project called Fostering Opportunity.

Carers get training, advice, dedicated support, a local fostering community and help from the service's therapeutic team, My Support Team. As part of the Foster Wales National Commitment, the same core training and support is promised by every council in Wales. The service holds information sessions around the borough, including sessions at Pontypool Active Living Centre and Cwmbran Stadium.

Across Wales the minimum weekly allowance for 2026-27 runs from £208 to £260 depending on the child's age, with any fee for the carer paid on top; ask each service what it pays above that. Our Wales page explains the national picture, and our Newport, Monmouthshire and Caerphilly pages cover the neighbouring areas. A good first step is to request an information pack from Foster Wales Torfaen and to talk to one or two of the services above.
